paper_metadata.title: Explicit block-encoding for partial differential equation-constrained optimization

summary: The paper proposes a fully coherent gate‑based algorithm for PDE‑constrained optimization combining a quantum PDE solver with quantum Hamiltonian descent via explicit block‑encoding of the objective function. Complexity analysis shows ~O(α_PDE d N^(η/d) M^3 T /(h_ξ^2 ε)) quantum gate complexity and predicts polynomial speedup in PDE system size N and evolution time T plus exponential speedup in spatial dimension d. Two proof‑of‑concept simulations (19‑qubit Black–Scholes calibration and 12‑qubit wave‑equation material design) validate the block‑encoding and optimization dynamics using Qiskit statevector simulation.

experiments.description: Numerical validation of the block-encoding and product-formula QHD optimization for parameter calibration in the Black-Scholes equation.

algorithm.variant: fully coherent PDE-constrained optimization using quantum Hamiltonian descent (QHD) with block-encoded objective and product-formula time evolution
algorithm.parameter_initialization: uniform superposition over discretized design variables via Hadamard gates

problem_formulation.encoding_details: volatility parameter σ encoded with 4 qubits as ξ in [0,1], with σ²=(σ²_max−σ²_min)ξ+σ²_min; objective is encoded via block-encoding of Ferr using forward-simulated PDE solution
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize Ferr(ξ)=||u(x,T;ξ)−u_ref||² subject to Black-Scholes PDE constraints
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: PDE constraint enforced by quantum forward simulation (LCHS/Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation); optimization via QHD on the encoded objective
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(s)= (1/(2λ(s)))Λ(M)+λ(s)F̂ with λ(s)=e^{νs}; objective operator F̂ derived from Ferr

problem_instance.description: Call-option volatility calibration in the Black-Scholes equation
problem_instance.dataset_name: European call option market data (reference price at selected x_ref)

dataset_specification.description: T=1, r=0.02, K=30, domain x∈[ln(10^-4), ln(10K)] discretized into 64 nodes; reference state built from analytical Black-Scholes formula at σ=0.3

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: domain truncation, finite-difference discretization, reference point chosen as x_ref closest to ln(Ke^{-r})
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: statevector simulation to validate block-encoding; optimization trajectory evaluated over 1000 product-formula iterations

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: finite-difference discretization; analytical Black-Scholes formula used to prepare reference state; mean objective value F̄ estimated for friction setting
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: objective expectation and standard deviation computed from simulated quantum states

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: expected objective decreases toward optimum with decreasing variance

implementation_details.evaluation_methodology: statevector simulation used to validate block-encoding circuits; time‑dependent Hamiltonian evolution implemented via direct classical matrix‑vector multiplication rather than quantum circuit simulation

classical_baselines.method_name: forward simulation with direct objective evaluation

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup in system size N, exponential speedup in spatial dimension d, polynomial speedup in evolution time T
speedup_claims.baseline_method: conventional classical PDE-constrained optimization with adjoint-based gradients
speedup_claims.conditions: under strong convexity and in the regime N >> M; speedup inherited from the underlying quantum PDE solver
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the end-to-end speedup is theoretical and depends on strong convexity; practical advantage is not established experimentally.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: ˜O(α_PDE d N^(η/d) M^3 T /(h_ξ^2 ε)) for the full algorithm under strong convexity; block-encoding objective evaluation ˜O(α_PDE d N^(η/d) M^2 m T log(1/ε)^(1/β))

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not provided; only asymptotic complexity comparison
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault‑tolerant quantum computer capable of implementing block‑encoded PDE solvers (QLSA/LCHS) and QHD with large N (discretized PDE size) and coherent time‑dependent Hamiltonian simulation
limiting_factors: Optimization dynamics simulated classically rather than as quantum circuits
Speedup depends on large PDE system size N and high spatial dimension d
Requires block‑encoded sparse‑matrix oracles and long coherent Hamiltonian simulation
Strong convexity assumption required for the convergence guarantee

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_statevector because the paper states Qiskit statevector simulation was used and no physical QPU is named.
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; only iteration count and gate-complexity expressions are given.
Paper explicitly frames advantages as asymptotic complexity improvements inherited from quantum PDE solvers rather than demonstrated empirical speedups.
All experiments are small‑scale numerical simulations validating algorithmic components.

experiments.description: Numerical validation of the block-encoding and product-formula QHD optimization for material parameter design in the one-dimensional wave equation.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: two design variables ξ1, ξ2 each encoded with 3 qubits; objective is encoded via block-encoding of the wave-energy functional (maximization converted to minimization by sign flip)
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize ∫_{3W/4}^{W} (c(x)^2 w(x,T)^2 + (∂w(x,T)/∂t)^2) dx, equivalently minimize its negative
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: PDE constraint enforced by quantum forward simulation of the discretized wave equation; maximization handled by replacing RP with −RP in the block-encoding
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(s)= (1/(2λ(s)))Λ(M)+λ(s)F̂ with λ(s)=e^{νs}; F̂=(Uobj+I)/2 for the maximization formulation

dataset_specification.description: domain length W=2^5−1, simulation time T=48, wave speeds c1=1 and c2=1/4, initial velocity v0 sparse Gaussian pulse, 5-qubit spatial grid plus one ancilla to encode the ODE

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: space discretization of the wave equation; sparse initial condition prepared by amplitude encoding
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: statevector simulation to validate block-encoding; optimization trajectory evaluated over 100 product-formula iterations

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: finite-difference discretization; sparse initial condition prepared by amplitude encoding; mean objective value F̄ estimated for friction setting
